messages.text: Man City lodge appeal against guilty verdict

metadata.summary: Manchester City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission finding them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules.
metadata.content: Man City lodge appeal: Premier League club contest guilty verdict of independent commission | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City lodge appeal: Premier League club contest guilty verdict of independent commission Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City have now lodged their appeal against the verdict; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023 Friday 2 October 2026 14:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol breaks down how long it may take for a final judgement to be reached following Man City's appeal against being found guilty of charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules Manchester City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission finding them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules. City insist in their statement they are "innocent" and have described the judgement against them as "opinion" and claimed it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe". The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Man City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m. messages.text: Vasseur admits 'big issue' with Ferrari distractions

metadata.content: Frederic Vasseur admits 'big issue' with Ferrari distractions at Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Frederic Vasseur admits 'big issue' with Ferrari distractions at Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia Ferrari's team principal says "sometimes the attacks are a bit personal" on him from external critics and "it's not good"; . watch final practice on Saturday at 5.30am with Qualifying for the Bahrain GP at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Friday 2 October 2026 12:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur says it is the 'right attitude' for his team to defend him against speculation surrounding his position. Frederic Vasseur says the "noise" surrounding Ferrari is a "big issue" for the team, admitting their release of a statement earlier this week reiterating the Italian outfit's faith in him had become "mandatory". Vasseur said after last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix that the team were "not working in perfect serenity" amid persistent and "frustrating" rumours around his position at the Scuderia. The Italian media have speculated over Vasseur's future in recent weeks amid links that Christian Horner would consider joining the team. City deny all charges. Gary Neville believes the ownership group at Manchester City will find it very difficult to "retain their status" at the club should the Premier League's ruling over financial breaches still stand following appeal. messages.text: Leclerc tops second practice in Malaysia but Red Bull impress

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc was fastest in second practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but Red Bull impressed during Friday's running.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Charles Leclerc tops second practice but Red Bull and Max Verstappen impress on Friday | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Charles Leclerc tops second practice but Red Bull and Max Verstappen impress on Friday Charles Leclerc topped second practice but Red Bull's Max Verstappen appears to have a slight advantage on the field; watch final practice on Saturday at 5.30am with Qualifying for the Bahrain GP at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event By Nigel Chiu in Sepang Friday 2 October 2026 13:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the Sepang International Circuit Charles Leclerc was fastest in second practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but Red Bull impressed during Friday's running. Leclerc was 0.099s quicker than Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, with McLaren's Lando Norris only 0.137s behind in a tight session which suggests four teams will have a shot at pole come qualifying on Saturday at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event . Max Verstappen was fourth but only 0.257s slower on the mediums, unusually deciding to not do a qualifying simulation on the softs.
